Mark terminal-NA cells with an explicit state label

Source: R/sequence_terminal.R
mark_terminal_state.Rd

mark_terminal_state() fills every missing cell after each sequence's last observed state with an explicit state, "End" by default, and returns the wide table. This turns right-censored sequences (drop-out, course end) into data for an absorbing-chain model: in a transition network built from the result with build_network(), the marked state is entered once a sequence stops and never left. Internal and leading missing cells are left as they are, and so are rows observed to the last position or not at all.

chain_structure() on that network gives the mean time to absorption, the absorption probabilities and each state's classification. markov_stability() is not the right summary for an absorbing chain: its stationary distribution collapses onto the absorbing state.

Usage

mark_terminal_state(data, state = "End", cols = NULL)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a matrix or data frame with one row per actor and one column per position, holding state labels, with NA for a missing observation. Without cols, the frame must be one column or a numbered run of positions (T1, T2, ...); other columns beside them raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

state

The label written into the trailing missing cells, a single non-empty string. Default "End". If the label already occurs in data, a warning is given and _1, _2, ... is appended until it is unique, so the absorbing marker is never confused with an observed state.

cols

The columns holding the positions, in order; only they are returned. A name not in data raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Default NULL (every column).

Value

A data frame of character columns with the shape of data (or of its cols), the trailing missing cells filled with the marker. The label used is kept in the "terminal_state" attribute, which differs from state when it had to be made unique. The columns are marked as positions, so build_network() reads them without state_cols.

Details

The marked state is absorbing because each sequence that reaches it stays there to the last column, so its only observed move is to itself (P[state, state] = 1 in a "relative" network). That needs at least one sequence with two or more trailing missing cells: when every sequence stops at most one cell early, the state has no outgoing transitions and its row in the network is zero.

Unlike build_network(end = ), which adds an end state only in the cell after each sequence's last observed state, with no outgoing edges and no self-loop, this function fills all the trailing cells.

See also

actor_endpoints(), chain_structure(), build_network()

Examples

M <- mark_terminal_state(trajectories, state = "Dropout")
net <- build_network(M, method = "relative")
chain_structure(net)
#> Chain structure  [4 states, 2 communicating classes]
#>   irreducible: FALSE   aperiodic: TRUE   regular: FALSE   reversible: NA
#>   recurrent classes: 1   transient classes: 1
#>   absorbing states: Dropout
#> 
#> Use summary(x) for the per-state table, plot(x) for the heatmap.
